prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right installer depends on your home, budget, equipment preference and whether you need ductwork, permitting or financing. I can help you pick the best contractor for your situation. To start, tell me:

- Your ZIP code (so I can narrow to companies that serve you)
- Type of home (single‑family, townhouse, apartment) and square footage
- Current system type (central AC, heat pump, ductless mini‑split) and age
- Any issues beyond the outdoor unit (ductwork, indoor coil, thermostat)
- Budget range and whether you want top efficiency (high SEER) or lower upfront cost
- Timeline (need it done now or can wait for estimates)

While you decide, here’s a practical checklist and guidance so you can quickly identify a trustworthy HVAC company:

What to require from any contractor
- Proper licensing and insurance: ask for license number and proof of liability insurance and workers’ comp. (Confirm local/state licenses apply in Georgia.)
- NATE‑certified technicians are a plus.
- Written estimate with itemized costs (equipment, labor, permits, disposal, refrigerant, ductwork).
- A Manual J load calculation (not a “rule of thumb”) to size the unit correctly; Manual D if ductwork changes are needed.
- Clear description of equipment make/model, SEER rating, and whether indoor coil and condenser are matched.
- Warranties: compressor and parts warranty length, and whether labor is covered and for how long.
- Permits and code compliance: the contractor should pull permits and handle inspections.
- Refrigerant handling: for older R‑22 systems confirm transition plan and price implications.
- References and recent customer reviews (Google, Yelp, Angi, BBB) — ask for local references if needed.
- Timeline and payment terms; avoid large upfront cash payments. Ask about financing options and rebates.

Questions to ask when getting estimates
- “Will you perform a Manual J load calculation?”  
- “What exact model, SEER rating and warranty does the estimate include?”  
- “Are indoor coil and condenser matched?”  
- “Is ductwork inspection included and would additional work be itemized separately?”  
- “Do you handle permits and inspections?”  
- “Who will perform the installation — your employees or subcontractors?”  
- “What is the estimated start and completion date?”  
- “Is there a written satisfaction or workmanship guarantee?”

Typical cost range (Atlanta area, ballpark)
- Basic central AC replacement (no ductwork changes): roughly $3,000–$7,500 depending on unit size and efficiency.
- High‑efficiency or heat pump systems and jobs requiring ductwork can be $7,000–$12,000+.
(Prices vary with equipment brand, SEER, labor rates and whether indoor equipment or ducts need replacement.)

How to pick between estimates
- Don’t choose solely by lowest price. Compare scope, equipment, sizing method, warranties, and included work.
- Prefer contractors who do Manual J and demonstrate understanding of your duct system and airflow.
- Ask for a breakdown of long‑term operating costs (higher SEER costs more up front but saves energy).

If you want, I can:
- Suggest several well‑rated installers near you (give ZIP), or
- Help compare 2–3 written estimates you receive and point out red flags.

Which would you like to do next?
